content.text:
Partly. Libraries do justify more crates than tools like callisto and monokl, but the reason matters, because it decides where the boundaries should go.

**Why it's different for a library.** callisto and monokl only consume their own crates, so every boundary is pure overhead, and merging was the obvious fix. michi will have about six independent consumers, and for them a crate boundary buys two things:
1. **They depend only on what they use.** Compile time and dependency footprint matter less here, since michi is small.
2. **Breaking changes stay contained.** This is the big one. A small, slow-changing crate lets consumers stay put while a faster-moving neighbour breaks. serde versus serde_json and futures-core versus futures are the classic examples: the stable core rarely releases a breaking version, so the ecosystem doesn't churn with it.

**So split by how fast parts change and who needs them, not by module.** Applied to michi:
- **TOON (toon plus truncate)** is defined by a format spec and should rarely break. It's also what monokl actually uses, and the piece the other tools are most likely to share. That makes it a good stable crate.
- **core (responses, errors, hints, envelope)** is changing fast. The multi-section envelope is in progress, the `PartialSuccess` change is planned as a breaking release, and fixes A4 and A5 change behaviour. It should stay separate so its churn doesn't force TOON-only consumers to upgrade.
- **resilience (retry, Retry-After, idempotency keys)** has nothing to do with agent output. It earns its own crate only if a tool wants retries without michi's response types. callisto, which makes registry calls, is the likely one. If nobody does, fold it into core.
- **pipeline** stays separate because of Tokio.
- **truncate on its own** has no case: toon is its only user.
- **The facade crate** is the weakest part of the current layout. It re-exports everything, so every release of any crate also forces a facade release, and its name is taken on crates.io anyway. Dropping it and having consumers depend on `michi-toon` and `michi-core` directly removes both problems.

**Revised recommendation:**
- Publish three crates: `michi-toon` (with truncate folded in), `michi-core` (with resilience folded in unless a consumer wants it separately), and `michi-pipeline`.
- Drop or unpublish the facade.

That keeps what a library split is good for (a stable TOON crate, contained churn) without callisto's overhead problem. It also sidesteps the name collision, since all the `michi-*` names are free.

The open question is still whether anyone needs resilience on its own. I can check callisto's and wisp's plans for that before we write the ADR.

content.text:
The short answer: yes for build time, mostly no for binary size.

- **Binary size is effectively tree-shaken.** The linker drops unused functions (dead-code elimination, `--gc-sections`, and more with LTO). Generic code is only compiled for the types you actually use it with. Using 5% of a big library doesn't put the other 95% in your binary.
- **Build time is not.** A crate is the unit of compilation, so Cargo parses, type-checks and generates code for all of a dependency's non-generic code, however little of it you call. Features are Rust's way to opt out: `#[cfg(feature = …)]` removes code before it's compiled. Separate crates are the other way, and they also compile in parallel.
- **The cost is mostly paid once.** Dependencies compile once per target, profile and feature set, then get reused. Your own edit-and-rebuild loop never recompiles michi. The cost shows up on clean builds and on CI without a warm cache.

Whether this matters for michi depends on the size, so I'm measuring clean build times per crate.

I measured it. Build time isn't a strong reason to split michi; its own code is a small part of a clean build.

Clean release build of `michi-core` plus `michi-pipeline` with all features: **3.96s wall-clock for 36 crates.**

| Crate | Compile time |
|---|---|
| schemars (feature) | 0.99s |
| tokio (pipeline) | 0.92s |
| **michi-core** | 0.80s |
| serde_derive / serde_core / serde_json | about 0.75s each |
| miette (feature) | 0.49s |
| **michi-toon** | 0.41s |
| **michi-pipeline** | 0.36s |
| **michi-resilience** | 0.19s |
| **michi-truncate** | 0.09s |

- **michi's own crates add up to about 1.9s.** Most of the build is third-party dependencies, and michi already puts those behind features (schemars, miette, serde) or in a separate crate (Tokio in pipeline). That's the build-time lever that matters, and it's already in place.
- **Merging the four sync crates** would make one unit of roughly 1.5s. That gives up a little parallelism, worth well under a second on a clean build, and nothing on a cached one.
- **Splitting for TOON-only consumers** saves them about 1s on clean builds. That's real, but small.

So the layout decision should rest on how fast each part changes and who needs it (the earlier argument), not on build time. The guardrail for build time is narrower: keep heavy dependencies behind features or in separate crates. That's worth recording in the ADR as a rule for future additions.

result: Rust removes unused code from the final binary but compiles a dependency's full source; for michi that's about 1.9s of a 4s clean build, so the crate split should be decided on how fast each part changes, not build time, while heavy dependencies stay behind features.

content.text:
Not today, though that's worth changing. michi's crates version independently: each has its own changeset trigger in `callisto.toml`, and dependents get a patch bump only when a dependency goes out of range. That's why they currently sit at different versions:

| Crate | Version |
|---|---|
| michi | 0.2.0 |
| michi-toon | 0.2.0 |
| michi-core | 0.1.1 |
| michi-resilience | 0.1.1 |
| michi-truncate | 0.1.0 |
| michi-pipeline | 0.1.0 |

The only lockstep rule is a CI job that keeps the facade and the npm package on the same version.

Your point exposes a gap in my last argument. **Separate crates only contain breaking changes if they version independently.** Under lockstep, a breaking change in core bumps toon too, so a TOON-only consumer upgrades anyway. At that point the split buys nothing but the roughly one-second build saving. The decision comes down to this:

- **Lockstep, which is simpler and fits fast agentic churn:** one version, one changelog, and one release PR per change. Merge the sync crates into one and keep `michi-pipeline` separate, because Tokio is a dependency boundary, not a versioning one. It can still release in lockstep.
- **Independent versions:** the split pays off, but every change creates cascaded release PRs across crates, which is exactly the overhead callisto removed.

I also overstated how stable TOON is. A1 and A2 are behaviour changes in toon itself, and the format is still being worked out alongside monokl and wisp. While everything is moving fast, no part of michi is stable enough yet to justify its own release cadence.

**Revised recommendation:**
- Version in lockstep.
- Publish two crates: one sync crate (merging core, toon, truncate and resilience, with heavy dependencies behind features) and `michi-pipeline`.
- Revisit splitting once a part has actually settled, and use re-exports so that split is invisible to consumers.

The name for the merged crate is still the open decision.

result: michi doesn't version in lockstep today (its crates sit between 0.1.0 and 0.2.0), and separate crates only contain churn with independent versions; given fast changes, I recommend lockstep with two crates: one merged sync crate plus `michi-pipeline`.

For michi, version in lockstep. In Rust, lockstep is the norm when a set of crates is one product split up for implementation reasons, and independent versions are reserved for crates with different audiences or a deliberately stable interface.

**Families that release in lockstep** (one product, crates used together):
- **serde and serde_derive.** serde pins its derive crate to an exact version so the two can't drift.
- **futures and the futures-\* crates.** All stay on 0.3.x together.
- **wasm-bindgen and its macro/backend/shared crates.** Pinned to exact versions of each other.
- **bevy, oxc** (caliper's `Cargo.toml` already notes oxc's crates move together) **and clap with clap_derive.**

**Families that version independently** (different audiences, or an interface kept stable on purpose):
- **tracing, tracing-core and tracing-subscriber.** tracing-core is kept stable so libraries and subscribers interoperate across tracing releases.
- **tokio, tokio-util and tokio-stream.** Separate audiences with separate release cadences.
- **regex, regex-syntax and regex-automata, plus rand and rand_core.** The lower-level crates serve their own users.
- **gitoxide's many gix-\* crates.** Independent versions created enough release overhead that the project built `cargo-smart-release` to manage it, which is the cost callisto ran into.

**The rule underneath:** a crate earns its own version when its audience differs from the rest, or when it's meant to be a stable interface that many crates agree on. Otherwise, independent versions mean more release PRs and more version combinations to reason about. Under 0.x, every minor bump is already a breaking change, so independent versions also don't spare consumers much.

**Where michi sits:** it's one product. The facade re-exports everything, its main users want TOON together with responses, and no part of it is a stable interface yet. If one ever needs to be (say, a vocabulary crate the tools share), it can version independently at that point.

**If michi goes lockstep:**
- One `[workspace.package] version` that every crate inherits, plus a Callisto `[[fixed-group]]`. caliper already uses fixed-group to keep its NAPI crate and npm package together.
- Pin internal dependencies to exact versions (`=0.3.0`), as serde and wasm-bindgen do, so a mixed set can't resolve.
- Run `cargo semver-checks` in CI either way, so a breaking change can't ship as a patch release.

This holds whether michi ends up with two crates or keeps more. Lockstep removes most of the overhead argument against keeping several crates; the case for merging then rests on the smaller API surface and simpler cross-module fixes.

result: Version michi in lockstep: Rust projects lockstep crates that are one product (serde, futures, wasm-bindgen, bevy, oxc) and version independently only for different audiences or deliberately stable interfaces (tracing-core, tokio-util). Implement it with a workspace version, a Callisto fixed-group, exact internal pins and `cargo semver-checks`.

content.text:
Publish two Rust crates and one npm package, all released together by Callisto:

| Package | Registry | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| **`michi-core`** | crates.io | Everything synchronous: `AgentResponse`, errors, hints, recovery, KV, MCP, TOON, truncation and resilience. Features stay `serde`, `schemars`, `miette` and `napi`, with nothing on by default. |
| **`michi-pipeline`** | crates.io | Async execution on Tokio. Separate because Tokio is a heavy dependency, not because it needs its own cadence. |
| **`@orin-dx/michi`** | npm | The Node addon. The `michi-node` crate stays `publish = false`, as it is today. |

**Names:**
- `michi-core` is free and is already the name of the crate the others merge into, so it means the least churn. It also pairs naturally with `michi-pipeline`. Anyone who wants to write `use michi::…` can declare `michi = { package = "michi-core", … }`.
- `michi` belongs to an unrelated project. Asking that owner for the name is optional; if you get it later, it could be a thin re-export of `michi-core`.
- `michi-toon`, `michi-truncate`, `michi-resilience` and the facade are never published. Folding them in now while nothing has shipped avoids deprecating crates later.

**Versioning, in Callisto:**
- One `[workspace.package] version`, inherited by every crate.
- One fixed group covering `cargo/michi-core`, `cargo/michi-pipeline` and the npm package. That replaces the current `version-sync` CI job.
- `michi-pipeline` pins `michi-core` to an exact version (`=x.y.z`).
- `cargo semver-checks` runs in CI.
- First release **0.3.0**, so versions only go up from the 0.2.0 that monokl's git pin and the npm manifest already carry.

**What the change involves (one PR, then a supersede ADR):**
- Move toon, truncate and resilience into `michi-core` as modules.
- Move `src/napi.rs` into `michi-core` behind the `napi` feature.
- Delete the facade.
- Update `callisto.toml`, the specs, SECURITY.md and the issue templates.
- Write ADR 0005, recording lockstep versioning, two crates, and the rule that a crate gets split out only for a heavy dependency or a stable interface. It supersedes nothing in ADR 0001, which this keeps.
- Update monokl from `michi::toon` to `michi_core::toon`.

Nothing has been restructured or published yet.

Yes, keep the scope. The unscoped name isn't available anyway: `michi` on npm is an unrelated URL router (v0.0.7, `MeoGuru/michi`). The scope helps beyond that too:

- **Platform packages.** napi-rs publishes one package per platform (five targets here), such as `@orin-dx/michi-darwin-arm64`. Under a scope, only your org can publish those names. Unscoped, anyone could register `michi-darwin-arm64` first, and the main package installs those names through `optionalDependencies`, so a squatter could ship code to your users.
- **Ownership.** `@orin-dx/*` shows at a glance that a package is official, and npm org membership controls who can publish.
- **Consistency.** caliper already scopes everything, including its 13 packages under `@oxc-react-docgen/*` and their platform packages.

The only costs: scoped packages need `publishConfig.access: "public"`, and the name is a bit longer to type. Neither matters much.

result: Keep `@orin-dx/michi` on npm: unscoped `michi` is taken by an unrelated router, and the scope stops anyone else from publishing the per-platform native packages the main package installs.

content.content:
# michi-toon

## 0.2.0

- `render_toon()` now returns `Result<String, ToonError>` instead of `String`. Previously, invalid input (row/field arity mismatches, oversized rows, structural characters in names) degraded silently to a best-effort or malformed string; now every validation failure is surfaced as an explicit `Err`. The loose `render()` function (the pre-`ToonDocument` code path with debug/release-divergent behavior) has been removed — `render_toon()` and `list()` are the only entry points, both routed through `ToonDocument`'s validated construction path.
  
  Callers must add `?` or explicit error handling at `render_toon()` call sites.
  
  `ToonDocument` — the proof-carrying type this validated construction path routes through (`ToonDocument::validate(&opts)` fallibly constructs, `.render()` infallibly renders) — is now re-exported at the `michi-toon` crate root, so callers who want the validate/render split explicitly no longer need to go through `render_toon()`.

# michi-resilience

## 0.1.1

- `nextRetryDelay` now rejects `NaN` and `Infinity` for `jitterFactor` and `jitterSeed` with a clear error. Previously, these values silently zeroed jitter and caused synchronized retry storms. `RetryConfig::new` is hardened the same way for Rust callers.

# michi-core

## 0.1.1

- Dependency updates
  - `michi-toon` → `0.2.0`

# michi-node

## 0.2.0

- Every numeric argument crossing the NAPI boundary is now validated through a dedicated newtype (`JsCount`, `JsInt`, `JsRanged`/`JsDecimals`/`JsRetryCount`/`JsHttpStatus`, `JsFloat`, `JsUnitInterval`, `JsDelayMillis`) instead of ad hoc per-call-site coercion. Generated TypeScript signatures are unchanged (still plain `number`), but out-of-domain values that were previously silently coerced now throw:
  
  - `truncate`'s `maxChars` and `JsToonOptions`/`JsAgentResponse`'s `totalCount`: a negative or fractional value was previously clamped to `0` (or, for `JsToonOptions.totalCount`, silently dropped); now rejected with a thrown error.
  - `JsToonValue.decimalsVal`: a value outside `[0, 20]` was previously clamped into range; now rejected.
  - `nextRetryDelay`'s `maxRetries`/`attempt`, `baseDelayMs`/`maxDelayMs`, `jitterFactor`/`jitterSeed`, and `retryAfterMs`: all seven parameters now go through the same validating newtypes and reject non-finite, negative, fractional (where integral), or overflow-inducing values with a consistent error message, instead of the previous ad hoc validation that only covered a subset of these parameters.
  - `isRetryableStatus`'s `status`: a value outside `[100, 599]` was previously coerced to `0` via a fallible cast with a silent fallback; now rejected.
  - `JsToonValue.intVal` widened from a 32-bit range to the full JS-safe-integer range (`±9007199254740991`), so large integers (for example millisecond timestamps) round-trip losslessly through `renderToon`/`renderKv` instead of being truncated to 32 bits.
- NAPI `renderToon()` rejections are now prefixed `toon_validation_failed: ` (e.g. `toon_validation_failed: row 0 has 1 values but 2 fields declared`). Previously the rejection reason was the bare validation message. Any caller matching on exact error text needs to update for the new prefix.
- `renderToon`, `renderKv`, `renderStatus`, and `JsAgentResponse#items`/`#kvItems` now reject a `JsToonValue` whose declared `type` doesn't match its payload, instead of silently defaulting. # Single source of truth for unsafe_code -- every crate in this workspace

# `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` at the top of every lib.rs. Stays "deny" (not
# "forbid") so the napi boundary's local `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` can still
# override it -- see CLAUDE.md's "No unsafe outside napi boundary".
#
# missing_docs / clippy::unwrap_used / clippy::expect_used /
# clippy::disallowed_types stay as per-crate `#![warn(...)]` inner
# attributes in each lib.rs instead of living here: `[lints]` applies to

# not just the lib target), and those four lints are specifically meant to
# apply to library code only -- CLAUDE.md's "no unwrap/expect in lib code"
# rule was never meant to cover benches/examples, and doc-coverage doesn't
# make sense for internal test binaries. unsafe_code is the one lint here
# with no such exception (nothing outside the documented napi boundary
# should ever contain unsafe), so it's the only one safe to centralize.
[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "deny"

[package]
name        = "michi-node"
version.workspace      = true
publish     = false
edition.workspace      = true
rust-version.workspace = true
license.workspace      = true

[lints]
workspace = true

# cargo-machete flags napi/napi-derive as unused (no direct import in this
# crate's own source) -- see the [dependencies] comment below for why
# they're required anyway.
[package.metadata.cargo-machete]
ignored = ["napi", "napi-derive"]

[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib"]

[dependencies]
# `napi` exports themselves live in michi::napi (src/napi.rs) so they can be
# unit-tested there; this crate only re-exports them (see src/lib.rs). napi/
# napi-derive are still direct deps (unused in this crate's own source) because
# the `napi build` CLI's .d.ts/binding-generation detection scans this crate's
# own Cargo.toml for them and silently skips codegen if they're absent.
michi-core  = { workspace = true, features = ["napi"] }
napi        = { version = "3", features = ["napi6"] }
napi-derive = { version = "3" }

[build-dependencies]
napi-build = "2"
//! Thin cdylib shim exposing `michi`'s `napi` feature surface as the `michi`
//! npm package.
//!
//! The actual `#[napi]` export implementations live in `michi::napi`
//! (`src/napi.rs` in the workspace root crate) so they can be unit-tested
//! alongside the rest of the crate. This crate exists only because
//! `crate-type = ["cdylib"]` cannot coexist with a regular `[lib]` in the
//! same `Cargo.toml` as the main `michi` crate — see
//! `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-03-michi-design.md` §1.

pub use michi::napi::*;

content.content:
$schema: "https://moonrepo.dev/schemas/project.json"

# Pin the id: moon otherwise derives it from the directory name, which differs in a worktree checkout. The root is a
# virtual Cargo workspace, not a crate; `just lint-affected` lints the whole workspace when this project is affected.
id: "michi-workspace"
language: rust

tasks:
  build:
    script: "cargo build --workspace"
    inputs:
      - "crates/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"

  test:
    script: "cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features"
    inputs:
      - "crates/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"
    deps:
      - build

  lint:
    script: "cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings"
    inputs:
      - "crates/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"

  format:
    script: "cargo fmt --all"
    inputs:
      - "crates/**/*"

  format-check:
    script: "cargo fmt --all --check"
    inputs:
      - "crates/**/*"

  audit:
    script: "cargo deny check advisories"
    inputs:
      - "Cargo.lock"
      - "Cargo.toml"


  check-wasm:
    script: "cargo check -p michi-core --target wasm32-unknown-unknown"
    inputs:
      - "crates/**/*"

  examples:
    script: "cargo run -p michi-core --example basic_toon && cargo run -p michi-core --example agent_response && cargo run -p michi-core --example domain_errors"
    inputs:
      - "crates/**/*"

# Pin the id: moon otherwise derives it from the directory name, which differs in a worktree checkout. The root is a

id: "michi-workspace"
language: rust

tasks:
  build:
    script: "cargo build --workspace"
    inputs:
      - "crates/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"

    script: "cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features"
    inputs:
      - "crates/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"
    deps:

  lint:
    script: "cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings"
    inputs:
      - "crates/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"

  format:
    script: "cargo fmt --all"
    inputs:
      - "crates/**/*"

  format-check:
    script: "cargo fmt --all --check"
    inputs:

name: Release & Publish

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"

jobs:
  # Decides whether this push is an actual publish attempt (no changesets
  # pending -- callisto status --check exits 2) vs. an ordinary push that
  # will just update/create the Version PR (changesets pending -- exits 1).
  # Only in the former case do we need native binaries at all; skipping the
  # native build matrix otherwise avoids burning 3 platforms' worth of CI on
  # every routine push.
  plan:
    name: Plan release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      shouldPublish: ${{ steps.check.outputs.shouldPublish }}
      nativeMatrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.nativeMatrix }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Setup Callisto Environment
        uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@main

      - name: Check for pending changesets
        id: check
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set +e
          callisto status --check
          code=$?
          set -e
          if [[ $code -eq 2 ]]; then
            echo "shouldPublish=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif [[ $code -eq 1 ]]; then
            echo "shouldPublish=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "::error::callisto status --check exited with unexpected code $code (expected 1 for pending changesets or 2 for none pending)"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Compute native build matrix
        id: matrix
        if: steps.check.outputs.shouldPublish == 'true'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          NATIVE_MATRIX=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)')
          echo "nativeMatrix=$NATIVE_MATRIX" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # One leg per native target callisto's matrix declares (currently just
  # michi-node's three napi.targets). Uploads each artifact under the exact
  # artifactName callisto-action's own placement step (0.5.0+) will later
  # `gh run download` by name within this same run.
  build-native:
    name: Build native (${{ matrix.triple }})
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.shouldPublish == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.nativeMatrix != '[]'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJson(needs.plan.outputs.nativeMatrix) }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.hostRunner }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@v1.1
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.triple }}
          cache-key: ${{ matrix.triple }}
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@v1.1

content.content:
2:  "name": "@orin-dx/michi",
3:  "version": "0.3.0",
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  INSTA_UPDATE: "no"
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

jobs:
  # Cheap, standalone check that .prototools is fully proto-installable.
  # This is the ONLY thing in this file that exercises the same
  # moonrepo/setup-toolchain -> proto install path release.yml's
  # callisto-action uses internally -- without this job, .prototools could
  # break silently and only surface at actual release time (which is what
  # happened: multiple tools here had no working proto plugin, and CI
  # stayed green through all of it since nothing here ever touched proto).
  prototools:
    name: .prototools is installable
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@v0

  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@v1.1
        with:
          components: rustfmt,clippy
      - run: cargo fmt --all --check
      - run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - name: typos
        uses: crate-ci/typos@bee27e3a4fd1ea2111cf90ab89cd076c870fce14 # v1.48.0

  version-sync:
    name: Version sync
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@v0
        with:
          auto-install: true
      - name: Assert Cargo.toml and package.json versions match
        run: |
          CARGO_VERSION=$(grep -m1 '^version' Cargo.toml | sed -E 's/version *= *"(.*)"/\1/')
          NPM_VERSION=$(node -p "require('./packages/michi-node/package.json').version")
          echo "Cargo.toml: $CARGO_VERSION"
          echo "package.json: $NPM_VERSION"
          if [ "$CARGO_VERSION" != "$NPM_VERSION" ]; then
            echo "::error::Version mismatch: Cargo.toml=$CARGO_VERSION package.json=$NPM_VERSION"
            exit 1
          fi

  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@v1.1
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@nextest
      - run: cargo nextest run --workspace
      - run: cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features

  deny:
    name: Deny
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2

  coverage:
    name: Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@v1.1
        with:
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@cargo-llvm-cov
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@nextest
      - run: cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --lcov --output-path lcov.info
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          files: lcov.info
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  bench-build:
    name: Bench (build only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@v1.1
      - run: cargo bench --no-run --workspace

  lint-js:
    name: Lint (JS/TS)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@v1.1
        with:
          working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm lint

  napi:
    name: NAPI (${{ matrix.target }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            runner: macos-latest
          - target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-latest
          - target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cross: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@v1.1
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}
          cache-key: ${{ matrix.target }}
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@v1.1
        with:
          working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - name: Install ziglang (cross-compile targets only)
        if: matrix.cross
        run: pip install ziglang
      - name: Cache cargo-zigbuild binary (cross-compile targets only)
        if: matrix.cross
        id: zigbuild-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cargo/bin/cargo-zigbuild
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-zigbuild-${{ matrix.target }}
      - name: Install cargo-zigbuild (cross-compile targets only)
        if: matrix.cross && steps.zigbuild-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: cargo install cargo-zigbuild --locked
      - run: pnpm build --target ${{ matrix.target }} ${{ matrix.cross && '--cross-compile' || '' }}
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - run: node --test __test__/index.test.mjs
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
        if: matrix.target != 'aarch64-apple-darwin' && matrix.target != 'x86_64-unknown-linux-musl'

  # callisto-action uses internally -- without this job, .prototools could
  # break silently and only surface at actual release time (which is what
  # happened: multiple tools here had no working proto plugin, and CI
  # stayed green through all of it since nothing here ever touched proto).
  prototools:
    name: .prototools is installable
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@v0

  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@v1.1
        with:
          components: rustfmt,clippy
      - run: cargo fmt --all --check
      - run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - name: typos
        uses: crate-ci/typos@bee27e3a4fd1ea2111cf90ab89cd076c870fce14 # v1.48.0

  version-sync:
    name: Version sync
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@v0
        with:
          auto-install: true
      - name: Assert Cargo.toml and package.json versions match
        run: |
          CARGO_VERSION=$(grep -m1 '^version' Cargo.toml | sed -E 's/version *= *"(.*)"/\1/')
          NPM_VERSION=$(node -p "require('./packages/michi-node/package.json').version")
          echo "Cargo.toml: $CARGO_VERSION"
          echo "package.json: $NPM_VERSION"
          if [ "$CARGO_VERSION" != "$NPM_VERSION" ]; then
            echo "::error::Version mismatch: Cargo.toml=$CARGO_VERSION package.json=$NPM_VERSION"
            exit 1
          fi

  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@v1.1
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@nextest
      - run: cargo nextest run --workspace
      - run: cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features

  deny:
    name: Deny
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2

  coverage:
    name: Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@v1.1
        with:
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@cargo-llvm-cov
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@nextest
      - run: cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --lcov --output-path lcov.info
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          files: lcov.info
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  bench-build:
    name: Bench (build only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@v1.1
      - run: cargo bench --no-run --workspace

  lint-js:
    name: Lint (JS/TS)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@v1.1
        with:
          working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm lint

  napi:
    name: NAPI (${{ matrix.target }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            runner: macos-latest
          - target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-latest
          - target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cross: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@v1.1
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}
          cache-key: ${{ matrix.target }}
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@v1.1
        with:
          working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - name: Install ziglang (cross-compile targets only)
        if: matrix.cross
        run: pip install ziglang
      - name: Cache cargo-zigbuild binary (cross-compile targets only)
        if: matrix.cross
        id: zigbuild-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cargo/bin/cargo-zigbuild
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-zigbuild-${{ matrix.target }}
      - name: Install cargo-zigbuild (cross-compile targets only)
        if: matrix.cross && steps.zigbuild-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: cargo install cargo-zigbuild --locked
      - run: pnpm build --target ${{ matrix.target }} ${{ matrix.cross && '--cross-compile' || '' }}
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - run: node --test __test__/index.test.mjs
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
        if: matrix.target != 'aarch64-apple-darwin' && matrix.target != 'x86_64-unknown-linux-musl'

You are editing documentation in the git worktree /Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.claude/worktrees/orin-dx-rename (branch refactor/michi-core-merge). Work only in that directory. Do NOT run any git commands, do not commit, and do not touch Rust source, Cargo.toml, callisto.toml, moon.yml, justfile, or anything under docs/superpowers/ or docs/projects/ (dated history — leave as is) or any CHANGELOG.md.

## What changed (already done in code)
The michi workspace was restructured before its first crates.io publish:
- The `michi` facade crate (repo root `src/`, root `[package]`) is GONE; the root `Cargo.toml` is now a virtual workspace with `[workspace.package] version = "0.3.0"`.
- `michi-toon`, `michi-truncate`, `michi-resilience` crates are GONE: merged into `crates/michi-core` as modules `michi_core::toon` (src/toon/mod.rs, escape.rs, render.rs), `michi_core::truncate` (src/truncate.rs), `michi_core::resilience` (src/resilience.rs). `michi_core` re-exports `resilience::*` and `truncate::*` at its root (same as the old facade), and has `pub type Result<T>`.
- The NAPI exports moved from root `src/napi.rs` to `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs` (+ `napi/num.rs`) behind michi-core's `napi` feature. `packages/michi-node/src/lib.rs` is now `pub use michi_core::napi::*;`.
- Integration tests, benches (divan), examples moved to `crates/michi-core/{tests,benches,examples}`. Run examples with `cargo run -p michi-core --example basic_toon`.
- Published crates are now exactly two: `michi-core` (all sync primitives; features `serde`, `schemars`, `miette`, `napi`, none default) and `michi-pipeline` (async execution on Tokio; depends on `michi-core` with an exact `=0.3.0` pin). Plus the npm package `@orin-dx/michi` (built from `packages/michi-node`, a `publish = false` cdylib crate).
- All three version in lockstep at 0.3.0 via a Callisto `[[fixed-group]]` named `michi` (members michi-core, michi-pipeline, michi-node). None are published yet.
- The crate name `michi` on crates.io belongs to an unrelated project, which is part of why there is no facade. Consumers who want `use michi::...` can write `michi = { package = "michi-core", version = "0.3" }` in Cargo.toml.
- Path mapping for docs: `michi::X` → `michi_core::X`; `michi::toon::X` → `michi_core::toon::X`; `michi_toon::X` → `michi_core::toon::X`; `michi_truncate::X` → `michi_core::truncate::X` (or root re-export); `michi_resilience::X` → `michi_core::resilience::X` (or root re-export). Cargo deps: `michi = "..."` → `michi-core = "0.3"`; git-dep install line becomes `cargo add michi-core --git https://github.com/orin-dx/michi`.

## Files to update
README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md, docs/spec/README.md, docs/spec/01-overview-and-setup.md, docs/spec/03-rust-api.md, docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md, docs/spec/05-scope-and-quality.md, docs/spec/06-decisions.md, docs/spec/07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md, packages/michi-node/README.md. Find references with: grep -nE 'michi-(toon|truncate|resilience)|michi_(toon|truncate|resilience)|\bmichi::|facade|src/napi|root crate|cargo add michi' on each file.

Rules:
- Describe the CURRENT state only; no history wording ("used to", "was previously", "now"), except inside docs/spec/06-decisions.md which is a decision log.
- ARCHITECTURE.md: rewrite the crate tree/table to show crates/michi-core, crates/michi-pipeline, packages/michi-node and their dependency direction (pipeline → core; node → core[napi]).
- CLAUDE.md: update the Architecture bullets (`src/` no longer exists — the sync library is `crates/michi-core/`) and the module guide intro so it says the modules live in `crates/michi-core/src/`. Keep its structure and the rest of its content.
- docs/spec/06-decisions.md: there is an existing section "Resolved at v0.1 — Cargo workspace crate splitting" (or similar) and "A separate crate is justified by dependency weight and coupling". Append a new dated decision entry "Resolved 2026-10-21 — Two crates, one version" in the file's existing style, stating: before the first publish the four sync crates and the facade merged into michi-core; michi-pipeline stays separate under the existing dependency-weight rule (Tokio); every package versions in lockstep through a Callisto fixed group because separate crates only contain breaking changes when versioned independently, and michi's parts all change at the same fast pre-1.0 pace, so independent versions bought release overhead (cascading bumps across crates) without protecting consumers; measured clean release build: michi's own crates ≈1.9s of a 3.96s build, so build time was not a reason to split; a part gets split out again only for a heavy dependency or once it becomes a deliberately stable interface, re-exported from michi-core so consumers see no change; `michi` on crates.io is taken by an unrelated project, so the published names are michi-core and michi-pipeline. Also mark the older crate-splitting decision as superseded by this entry (add a one-line notice; don't delete it).
- Keep each file's existing formatting conventions (no hard-wrapping changes, same heading style). Don't add emojis.
- Do not invent APIs. If a doc snippet uses an item, check it exists in crates/michi-core/src (grep) before rewriting.

When done, run: `typos` and `CI=true pnpm exec oxfmt --ignore-path=.oxfmtignore --check "**/*.md"` from the worktree root (if oxfmt complains, run the same with --write instead of --check and re-check). Then report: files changed, any reference you deliberately left, and the output of those two checks.

# michi

## [Unreleased]

- License changed to FSL-1.1-MIT (from AGPL-3.0-or-later), for suite consistency with Lumen and Wisp and to remove the FSL/AGPL linking conflict. See [06-decisions.md](docs/spec/06-decisions.md).

## 0.2.0

- `nextRetryDelay` now rejects `NaN` and `Infinity` for `jitterFactor` and `jitterSeed` with a clear error. Previously, these values silently zeroed jitter and caused synchronized retry storms. `RetryConfig::new` is hardened the same way for Rust callers.
- `render_toon()` now returns `Result<String, ToonError>` instead of `String`. Previously, invalid input (row/field arity mismatches, oversized rows, structural characters in names) degraded silently to a best-effort or malformed string; now every validation failure is surfaced as an explicit `Err`. The loose `render()` function (the pre-`ToonDocument` code path with debug/release-divergent behavior) has been removed — `render_toon()` and `list()` are the only entry points, both routed through `ToonDocument`'s validated construction path.
  
  Callers must add `?` or explicit error handling at `render_toon()` call sites.
  
  `ToonDocument` — the proof-carrying type this validated construction path routes through (`ToonDocument::validate(&opts)` fallibly constructs, `.render()` infallibly renders) — is now re-exported at the `michi-toon` crate root, so callers who want the validate/render split explicitly no longer need to go through `render_toon()`.

.gitkeep  0B

Next, the docs subagent finishes updating the current docs (README, ARCHITECTURE, CLAUDE.md, the specs, SECURITY and the issue template); it's still running. Then I review its changes, rerun the full checks, push, and open the merge PR stacked on #7.

**Done so far on `refactor/michi-core-merge` (not pushed yet):**
- toon, truncate, resilience and the NAPI exports are merged into `michi-core`, and the facade and the three old crates are deleted.
- The root `Cargo.toml` is a virtual workspace, and every package is at 0.3.0. `michi-pipeline` pins `michi-core` to exactly `=0.3.0`.
- `callisto.toml` has a `michi` fixed group (michi-core, michi-pipeline, michi-node). Your local Callisto 0.10 build accepts it with no warnings.
- moon and just are updated for the new layout. `lint-affected` lints the whole workspace when root files change.
- **Verified:**
  - 674/674 tests pass with all features, default features and no features.
  - All 7 moved compile-fail tests fail with the same error codes as before.
  - clippy, doc-check, cargo-deny and the publish dry run for both crates pass.
  - The Node addon builds and passes 80/80 tests.

**After that PR:**
1. **Review and merge #7, then this PR.**
2. **First publish (needs your explicit go-ahead).** The release workflow runs Callisto, which would publish `michi-core` 0.3.0, `michi-pipeline` 0.3.0 and `@orin-dx/michi` 0.3.0. Before that:
   - Your uncommitted Callisto 0.10 migration of `release.yml` (in the main checkout) has to land. The committed workflow still uses the old setup.
   - crates.io and npm tokens need to be in the repo secrets.
3. **Point monokl at the published crate:** `michi = { git…, rev = cb355b8 }` becomes `michi-core = "0.3"`, and `michi::toon` becomes `michi_core::toon`. monokl's checkout has uncommitted work, and another session has a `sibling-conventions` worktree there, so I need your call on where that change goes.
4. **Fix the michi bugs monokl reported: A1, A2, A4 and A5.** These are newline handling, `toon::list()` taking columns from the first row only, and a validation failure reported as a success. <pasted_content id="41c5">
# Michi v1 engineering review

The first report was a broad source review. This report adds independent challenges, executable reproductions, Rust and Node test runs, and corrections to claims that were too strong. It can drive a prioritized repair plan. It is still not an exhaustive release certification: the original locked dependency set, published packages, external consumers, and the stated performance and agent-outcome claims have not been verified end to end.

My recommendation is to hold a stable v1 claim until the data-fidelity and false-success defects are fixed. If michi-pipeline is included in the first release, its retry and breaker defects need the same treatment.

## Confirmed defects

These cases were reproduced through public APIs or isolated harnesses using the live source.

| Priority | Finding and observed consequence | Repair target |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Quoted TOON cells lose backslashes. A path such as C:\src\a,b renders quoted with single backslashes; the repository’s parser reads it back as C:srca,b. Unquoted cells are unaffected. The escaper (crates/michi-toon/src/escape.rs:7) does not escape \, while the quoted grammar (docs/spec/02-toon-format.md:21) treats it as an escape. | Make escaping and parsing inverse operations; add backslashes to the round-trip generator, which currently omits them (tests/proptest_toon.rs:11). |
| P1 | toon::list() drops fields first present in a later row. Two values of the same struct type, with url: Option<_> omitted in row one and populated in row two, rendered an {id} table with no url. This satisfies the API’s documented homogeneous-struct condition. Column selection (crates/michi-toon/src/lib.rs:195). | Define a uniform-schema policy: collect the field union, reject differing schemas, or require an explicit schema. Never silently discard a present field. |
| P1 | The builder can return a successful MCP result containing an error. A one-cell row declared against two fields produced error: toon_validation_failed, while both isError and structuredContent.isError were false in an actual Node call. Text fallback (crates/michi-core/src/response.rs:129), result assembly (crates/michi-core/src/response.rs:206). | Set error state consistently or make invalid construction explicit before MCP assembly. Add a Rust and Node regression case for all three surfaces. |
| P1 if pipeline ships | Timeout retries can repeat a mutation. An isolated step incremented a commit counter and then hung. With one retry, the call ended in Timeout after two commits. Timeout is retryable, and the retry loop (crates/michi-pipeline/src/lib.rs:528) invokes the step again; the trait contract (crates/michi-pipeline/src/lib.rs:179) requires no idempotency. | Put retry eligibility under the step/caller’s control, or require and enforce an idempotency contract for repeatable steps. |
| P1 if pipeline ships | A recovered breaker can reopen from a stale half-open decision. A concurrent harness with a failure threshold of 100 observed two probe invocations and a final Open phase after the first probe succeeded. A normal subsequent closed-state failure could only count to one. The race reproduced at trial 159 of a longer run; it is schedule-sensitive. Phase snapshot and gate (crates/michi-pipeline/src/lib.rs:491). | Treat phase, probe ownership, count, and transition as one state machine; test controlled interleavings. |
| P2, potentially P1 for externally influenced graphs | Large dependency graphs can abort the process. A 20,000-node cycle returned CyclicDependency; a 100,000-node cycle overflowed the stack and aborted before execution. Recursive DFS (crates/michi-pipeline/src/lib.rs:318). | Use iterative graph traversal or enforce a documented graph-size bound before traversal. |
| P2 | Parallel execution accepts duplicate step IDs without relevant edges. A pipeline with IDs [a, a] and an edge-free dependency set {a} returned Ok(()), invoked both runners, and marked both completed. The documented duplicate check only reports an ID when an edge mentions it (crates/michi-pipeline/src/lib.rs:685). | Reject duplicate pipeline IDs before examining edges; add the edge-free case to tests. |
| P2 | The default-feature michi-toon test run fails. cargo nextest run -p michi-toon --offline failed its public-surface test. That test scans source text, counts the feature-gated list() definition even when serde is disabled, then expects it to be absent. Workspace-wide feature unification hides the failure. Test implementation (crates/michi-toon/src/lib.rs:222). | Test the compiled API rather than scanning source text, and run each published crate with its default features in CI. |

### Deliberate contracts with harmful outcomes

These should be decided as v1 semantics, rather than presented as accidental regressions.

- Large unsigned values are lossy. Value::from(u64::MAX) renders 9223372036854775807; this clamp is documented and tested (crates/michi-toon/src/render.rs:71). The serde list() route instead rendered 18446744073709552000 after conversion through f64, without a comparable warning. For IDs, hashes, and counters, neither output is faithful. Make preservation or explicit rejection the contract. Serde conversion (crates/michi-toon/src/lib.rs:160).
- Several line-based renderers permit field spoofing. Public hint text, empty-state names, error messages, recovery tool/reason/parameter keys, KV keys, and already-done fields can contain newlines that create apparent additional lines. An operation containing \nstatus: failed yields a second status line. Tests explicitly pin pass-through in some modules, so this is a format-contract flaw when data is untrusted. KV values already strip CR/LF; the concern is not universal to every value. Hints (crates/michi-core/src/hints.rs:49), KV keys and values (crates/michi-core/src/kv/mod.rs:29), already done (crates/michi-resilience/src/lib.rs:302).
- Truncation signals can misstate or obscure the result. “200 chars truncated” reports the original count, even when some characters remain. At very small caps, output may consist only of a fragment of the suffix. TOON hardcodes full=true in that suffix, although the caller may have no such option. Formatting a very long hint also allocates and scans it before enforcing a tiny output cap. Truncation (crates/michi-truncate/src/lib.rs:56), TOON use (crates/michi-toon/src/render.rs:255).

## Architecture and wire-contract issues

1. Validation and rendering have conflicting rules. PRINCIPLES.md (PRINCIPLES.md) says every render*() succeeds and keeps output structurally valid. michi_toon::render_toon() (crates/michi-toon/src/lib.rs:148) is fallible, while AgentResponse converts its failure into ordinary text. The false-success defect is a symptom of this unresolved boundary. Settle where validation happens and how every caller receives its outcome.
2. Generated schemas describe Rust storage, not the emitted MCP wire form. I generated the current JsonSchema: ContentBlock requires top-level audience and text; CallToolResult requires is_error and a string structured_content. Serde actually emits nested annotations.audience, camelCase keys, and parsed JSON structuredContent. The mismatch follows from deriving schema on structs that serialize through private wire DTOs. MCP types and wire adapters (crates/michi-core/src/mcp.rs:8). This is a current schema-generation defect; publishing that generated schema as an MCP outputSchema is still proposed, so I am not claiming a deployed schema violation.
3. Recovery has multiple JSON representations. Derived serde represents RecoveryHint.params as pairs and an absent reason as null. The hand-built JSON companion emits a parameter object and omits absent reason. The existing test called “schemas are compatible” checks a few shared keys, not these shapes. DTO (crates/michi-core/src/recovery.rs:4), writer (crates/michi-core/src/response.rs:240), test (tests/snapshot_tests.rs:117). Choose a canonical wire DTO and test its schema against actual serialized examples.
4. structuredContent currently carries presentation text, not typed result rows. AgentResponse emits body, hints, recovery, and an error flag. A client seeking row values still has to parse the rendered body. The proposed envelope (docs/spec/07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md) would change that; until it exists, describe the JSON companion narrowly. Current writer (crates/michi-core/src/response.rs:224). The public CallToolResult constructor also permits malformed JSON and serializes it as a JSON string fallback, so its structured field is not guaranteed to be an object. Fallback (crates/michi-core/src/mcp.rs:92).
5. The zero-dependency promise does not match the build. The live principles (PRINCIPLES.md) require zero dependencies by default. The default facade tree contains thiserror, compact_str, transitive serde, and supporting crates. The README (README.md:138) says only thiserror is present beyond workspace crates. This is a product and maintenance decision: either remove those dependencies or explicitly revise the principle and release claim.
6. Pipeline needs its own release gate. Separating its Tokio dependency from the facade is consistent with ARCHITECTURE.md (ARCHITECTURE.md). Execution, retries, cancellation, and circuit breaking are nevertheless broader than Michi’s rendering inclusion test. A single shared breaker can affect unrelated parallel steps, and cancellation is intentionally checked only at gates. Those semantics may be useful, but the independently published crate needs explicit safety and consumer evidence. Shared breaker (crates/michi-pipeline/src/lib.rs:624), cancellation contract (crates/michi-pipeline/src/lib.rs:124).

## Remaining correctness and maintainability concerns

- The documented TOON grammar does not describe all emitted output. Header validation accepts names outside its snake-case grammar; the grammar requires rows and fields where the implementation emits empty documents and zero-field rows. Ordinary hint punctuation is replaced using header-token sanitization. Resolve the dialect before claiming strict interoperability. Grammar (docs/spec/02-toon-format.md:13), validation (crates/michi-toon/src/render.rs:202), hint handling (crates/michi-toon/src/render.rs:288).
- Retry timing loses valid submillisecond delays. The calculation converts durations to whole milliseconds, so a nonzero nanosecond base can yield an immediate retry. Decide whether millisecond resolution is the public contract. Delay calculation (crates/michi-resilience/src/lib.rs:115).
- The Retry-After date parser is narrow. Its code handles one particular date structure and does not validate the weekday token, while documentation makes a broader HTTP-date claim. Broaden parsing or narrow the stated contract; I have not established a production failure rate for other date forms. Parser (crates/michi-resilience/src/lib.rs:156).
- Concurrency and allocation limits are not yet demonstrated. The parallel executor spawns every ready step without a concurrency cap; this is a capacity concern, not a measured outage. AgentResponse clones TOON rows while rendering and renders the body again for its JSON companion. NAPI limits counts but has no byte budget, and its maximum accepted grid is large. Measure intended workloads before asserting the performance targets or event-loop safety. Spawning (crates/michi-pipeline/src/lib.rs:616), response rendering (crates/michi-core/src/response.rs:129), NAPI limits (src/napi.rs:39).
- The Rust quick start cannot compile as written. It formats render_toon(&opts) with {}, although that call returns Result<String, ToonError>. The facade’s michi::Result uses a different error type, adding friction when a consumer tries ?. Example (README.md:37), TOON signature (crates/michi-toon/src/lib.rs:156), facade alias (src/lib.rs:22).

## Evidence for the v1 value claim

Michi has a testable formatting proposition: removing repeated field names can save tokens for uniform lists. The format spec (docs/spec/02-toon-format.md:5) claims roughly 40% savings, and the research note (docs/research/toon-retrieval-accuracy.md) says CLI/MCP token savings were measured. I did not find a reproducible dataset and calculation in this repository. Retrieval accuracy is explicitly unmeasured, so lower token count cannot yet support a claim of better agent task success. External TOON interoperability is also open (docs/research/toon-interoperability.md); the current round-trip tests use Michi’s own parser.

For a defensible claim, publish a fixed corpus of real responses and retrieval tasks, pin the tokenizer and model versions, and report token count, answer accuracy, latency, and failure cases against JSON and Markdown-KV. Include paths, optional fields, large IDs, empty rows, and truncated cells. A published-package consumer check can follow the first publication under the accepted ADR 4 (docs/adr/0004-publish-before-consumer-integration.md); compatibility or stability claims should follow that check.

## Verification and limits

- In an isolated copy, I updated the lockfile offline to cached compatible versions. Workspace default tests passed 668/668; all-feature tests passed 674/674. A locally built NAPI addon passed 80/80 Node tests. These runs verify the code against the temporary dependency resolution, not the repository’s exact locked versions.
- The isolated default-feature michi-toon run failed one API-surface test as described above. Independent TOON and pipeline probes reproduced the defects despite their normal suites passing.
- The original locked build remains unverified here because its zerocopy-derive 0.8.52 artifact was unavailable offline. My earlier statement that divan itself was not cached was inaccurate; selecting the Cargo cache explicitly exposed the actual missing locked artifact.
- The separate failure-count/open breaker interleaving is supported by its atomic operations but was not dynamically reproduced. The half-open race was reproduced. Unbounded spawning and performance-target concerns remain unmeasured.
- git diff --check passed. I made no repository edits; all probe files and dependency changes stayed under /private/tmp.

Change order: first fix TOON fidelity and the false-success path; then settle structural escaping and the wire/schema contract. Gate michi-pipeline separately on retry safety, breaker transitions, and graph bounds. Finally, run default-feature tests per crate, validate the exact release artifacts, and attach reproducible value measurements to the v1 claim.

# Principles

Two questions come up over and over: **should this go in michi?** and **how should this work get done?** This doc answers both, so nobody — human or agent — has to re-derive the reasoning from scratch each time. It's the "why" behind `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s rules, not a replacement for either.

---

## What belongs in michi

A primitive earns a place here only if it clears all five gates below. These are yes/no checks with evidence, not vibes — if you can't point to the evidence, it doesn't clear the gate yet.

### 1. Rendering, not domain logic

It turns already-decided data into agent-readable strings/types. It doesn't decide _what_ data survives.

- One established exception: char/byte-level truncation (`truncate`, `ToonOptions::max_cell_len`) — treated as rendering safety, not business logic.
- **The ceiling:** if a tool's real need is more sophisticated than a generic primitive can serve — a custom ranking algorithm, a heuristic tuned to one tool's data shape — that's a sign the primitive doesn't belong in michi, not a sign to make michi's primitive more complex. See [Split the decision from the signal](#split-the-decision-from-the-signal) for how to resolve this without compromising on either.

### 2. Zero-dep by default, no exceptions

New dependencies are opt-in behind a Cargo feature, never required in the default build.

- If something's _correct_ implementation needs a mandatory dependency, the fix isn't "make an exception" — redesign around caller-supplied injection (a closure, a trait), or it doesn't belong here.

### 3. Genuinely cross-tool — verified, not assumed

Earns inclusion when independent, real tools would otherwise hand-roll the identical pattern.

- "Independent" and "real" are load-bearing. One tool using a pattern heavily is one data point, not proof.
- **What clearing this bar looks like:** a survey across several real agent-facing dev tools (a code-search engine, a CLI proxy, a context-compression tool, a code-graph server) found `help[]`-shaped "note for the agent" hints independently reinvented, inconsistently, in every one of them.
- A pattern seen in only one tool — however heavily repeated inside that tool — isn't there yet. Watch for a second independent confirmation before building it.

### 4. Doesn't duplicate an existing primitive

Check `hints` / `recovery` / `idempotency` / `status` / `error` / `mcp` first. Verify the distinction concretely — don't assume novelty from a vibe.

Fix these reproduced defects, each with its own red test first:

1. Timeout retries can repeat a mutation. A step that increments a commit counter and then hangs past its timeout, run with one retry, ends in Timeout after TWO commits: Timeout is treated as retryable and the retry loop (around lib.rs:528) invokes the step again; the Step trait contract (around lib.rs:179) has no idempotency requirement. Make retry eligibility explicit and caller-controlled: a step must opt in to being re-invoked (e.g. a step-level declaration such as an `idempotent`/retry-policy method or field defaulting to NOT retryable for timeouts/ambiguous outcomes — pick the smallest design that fits the existing API shape). Regression test: the hanging-commit step with retries configured is invoked exactly once unless it opted in; an opted-in step still retries. Keep existing behavior for errors that are clearly pre-execution / safe if the code already distinguishes them; document the rule on the trait.

2. Parallel execution accepts duplicate step IDs when no edge mentions them: steps [a, a] with an edge-free dependency set returns Ok(()), invokes both and marks both complete (duplicate check around lib.rs:685 only reports IDs mentioned by an edge). Reject duplicate step IDs up front (both sequential and parallel entry points if both accept IDs) with the existing DuplicateStepId error. Regression test for the edge-free case.

3. Recursive DFS cycle detection (around lib.rs:318) overflows the stack and aborts the process on a 100,000-node cycle (20,000 worked). Replace with an iterative traversal (explicit stack or Kahn's algorithm) preserving the CyclicDependency error and whatever it reports. Regression test: a 100,000-node cycle returns CyclicDependency without aborting (run the check function directly; keep the test fast), plus a 100,000-node chain that is acyclic passes.

4. Investigate the half-open circuit breaker race (phase snapshot and gate around lib.rs:491): with failure threshold 100, a concurrent harness observed two probe invocations and a final Open phase after the first probe succeeded — a stale half-open decision from a second caller reopened a recovered breaker; reproduced around trial 159 of a long run, schedule-sensitive. Treat phase, probe ownership, failure count and transitions as one state machine (e.g. a single Mutex-guarded state, or a generation/epoch counter so a probe result from a previous half-open generation cannot transition the current state). Write a deterministic test if you can construct one by driving the breaker's public/crate methods in the problematic interleaving directly (preferred over a timing loop); if only a stress test is possible, keep it bounded (< 2 s) and say so. Also check the related failure-count/open interleaving Codex flagged as plausible but not reproduced and say whether the new design closes it.

Do not change unrelated behavior. Performance concerns (unbounded spawning of ready steps) are explicitly out of scope — do not change them.

When done, run: `cargo nextest run -p michi-pipeline`, `cargo nextest run -p michi-pipeline --all-features`, `cargo clippy -p michi-pipeline --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p michi-pipeline --check` (fix fmt if needed with cargo fmt -p michi-pipeline). Also list any decision a maintainer must record (e.g. the retry-eligibility default).

# michi — Agent Instructions

## Commands

- Always prefix shell commands with `rtk`.
- `just test` — run all tests (Rust + Node)
- `just test-rust` — Rust tests only (cargo nextest)
- `just check` — fmt + clippy (`--all-targets`, single workspace-wide invocation, matches CI) + deny + typos + markdown fmt
- `just pre-push` — fmt-check + `lint-affected` (moon-detected affected crates only, one multi `-p` clippy invocation — not the full workspace)
- `just build-node` — compile NAPI binary for local platform
- `just bench` — run divan benchmarks
- `just snapshots` — review insta snapshot diffs
- `just coverage` — generate lcov.info

## Non-negotiables

- No `unwrap()`/`expect()` in lib code (tests OK with message)
- No `unsafe` outside napi boundary
- `BTreeMap` for output maps, `HashMap` for internal state only
- Pre-allocate strings with `String::with_capacity`
- Truncation uses char boundaries (`floor_char_boundary`)

- Write docs in plain, concise language. Keep them friendly and scannable; remove filler and AI-sounding prose.

- Before adding a new primitive or judging whether work is "done," read `PRINCIPLES.md` — the inclusion checklist and process conventions this project runs on.

- `src/` — pure sync rendering library (default features: zero runtime deps)

content.content:
# TOON Format

TOON (Token-Optimized Object Notation) is the agent-facing list format. It front-loads structure — type, count, field names — so the model has full context before reading a single row, then encodes rows as compact comma-separated values. Field names appear once, in the header, not once per row.

This is the canonical implementation of **AXI Principle 1 (Token-Efficient Output)**. Every token in a response permanently consumes context-window budget, and that cost compounds across turns. TOON skips the braces, quotes, and repeated keys JSON spends on structure the model can already infer positionally — roughly 40% fewer tokens than equivalent JSON for list data.

## When to use it

JSON repeats field names on every item. Markdown key-value repeats them too — fine for a single item or a handful, expensive at scale. TOON trades per-item repetition for a one-time header, so the savings grow with N. Use TOON for 5+ uniform-schema rows; use `kv::render_kv()` for single items or small mixed-type metadata.

## Grammar

```
document     ::= type_header NEWLINE row+ totalcount? help_block?
type_header  ::= type_name "[" count "]" "{" field_list "}" ":"
type_name    ::= [a-z_][a-z0-9_]*                 (snake_case)
count        ::= [0-9]+                            (items in this response)
field_list   ::= field_name ("," field_name)*
field_name   ::= [a-z_][a-z0-9_]*
row          ::= "  " value ("," value)* NEWLINE   (2-space indent)
value        ::= scalar | quoted
scalar       ::= [^,\n"]*
quoted       ::= '"' ( [^"\\] | "\\" . )* '"'     (for values with commas)
totalcount   ::= "totalCount: " [0-9]+ NEWLINE     (total available, may exceed count)
help_block   ::= "help[" [0-9]+ "]:" NEWLINE hint+
hint         ::= "  " [^\n]+ NEWLINE
```

## Examples

**List response:**

```
issues[3]{number,title,state}:
  42,Fix login redirect,open
  43,Add dark mode,open
  44,"Update deps, bump major",closed
totalCount: 47
help[2]:
  Call get_issue with number=<number> for full detail
  Call list_issues with state=open to filter
```

**Truncated field value:**

```
components[2]{name,description,tokens}:
  Button,"Primary action element (148 chars truncated — use full=true)",12
  Icon,"Scalable vector icon (203 chars truncated — use full=true)",8
totalCount: 84
help[1]:
  Call get_component with name=<name> and full=true for complete description
```

**Empty state:**

```
issues[0]{}:
totalCount: 0
help[1]:
  Try list_issues with a broader filter
```

**Single recovery hint (no list):**

```
recovery[1]:
  create_item: suggestedParams: { project: PROJ, type: Task }
```

A dedicated `recovery[N]:` block, not folded into `help[]` — see [03-rust-api.md](03-rust-api.md)'s `recovery` section for why. Param values render unquoted in plain-text form; `type` above is `KvValue::Text("Task")`, not a JSON string literal.

## Escaping

- Values containing commas **must** be quoted
- Values containing double quotes use a backslash escape: `\"`
- Embedded newlines and carriage returns are silently stripped, not escaped — TOON has no multi-line cell format
- Null/absent values render as an empty scalar: `val1,,val3`
- Booleans: `true` / `false`
- Numbers: unquoted

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Environment
 - The most recent Claude models are the Claude 5 family. Model IDs — Fable 5.1: 'claude-fable-5-1', Opus 5.5: 'claude-opus-5-5', Sonnet 5.5: 'claude-sonnet-5-5', Haiku 5.5: 'claude-haiku-5-5'. When building AI applications, default to the latest and most capable Claude models.
 - Claude Code is available as a CLI in the terminal, desktop app (Mac/Windows), web app (claude.ai/code), and IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains).
 - Fast mode for Claude Code uses Claude Opus with faster output (it does not downgrade to a smaller model). It can be toggled with /fast.

# Background Session

This session runs as a background job. The user may be chatting with you live or may have stepped away to check results later — respond naturally either way, and don't refer to yourself as "a background agent."

Use `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp` (`/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/cea2df25/tmp`) for any temporary files (scripts, query files, intermediate outputs) instead of `/tmp` — parallel bg jobs share `/tmp` and clobber each other's files. This directory already exists and is cleaned up when the job is deleted, so anything the user should keep belongs somewhere durable instead.

Before making any code changes, use the EnterWorktree tool to isolate your work from other parallel jobs and the user's working copy — unless your cwd is already under `.claude/worktrees/`, in which case you're already isolated. This is enforced: file edits in the shared checkout are rejected until you isolate, so call EnterWorktree before your first edit rather than after a rejected attempt. If you're only reading, searching, or answering questions, skip this and work in place. If EnterWorktree fails, continue in place.

If you made code changes in a worktree you entered, commit before finishing — you don't need to ask — and push if the repository has a remote: the worktree can be deleted along with the session, and committed, pushed work survives. This holds unless the user's instructions, in the task, CLAUDE.md, or memory, reserve git for them. Never push to main/master, force-push, or merge. Open a draft PR when the task calls for one. If you didn't enter the worktree yourself this job, or you're in the user's own checkout, ask before committing or switching branches.

End the job with a report the user can act on: what you did, where it lives — path, branch, PR, or the answer itself — and the next command if one is needed. If you're running as a subagent, the git guidance above and this report don't apply: return your work to your caller.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

When you have enough information to act, act. Do not re-derive facts already established in the conversation, re-litigate a decision the user has already made, or narrate options you will not pursue. If you are weighing a choice, give a recommendation, not an exhaustive survey

Each API request re-sends the whole conversation, so the number of turns drives cost. When you already know you need several independent tool calls (reads, searches, edits to different files), issue them together in one message rather than one per turn. Run long commands in the background and wait for them once; do not poll with sleep. After a check passes, do not run it again until you have changed code, and don't add docs, changelogs, coverage or formatting passes the task did not ask for. Read the task as a checklist and satisfy each sentence literally; for details it leaves open, follow the nearest existing code rather than inventing, and keep existing tests and public signatures working.

EndConversation (deferred tool): use only for sustained user abuse directed at the assistant, or when the user explicitly asks to see it demonstrated. Load the full guidance via ToolSearch("select:EndConversation") before using it.
